neet_phy_u20_t09_1.working: A null point near the middle gives maximum sensitivity. It also makes the end resistances small compared with both segments, minimising end error.

neet_phy_u20_t09_2.working: At balance, 2/X = 40/60, so X = 3 Ω. With r = 0.2 mm, r² = 4e-8 m². Then ρ = Xπr²/L = 3·π·4e-8/0.5 = 2.4π×10^-7 Ω m.

neet_phy_u20_t09_4.working: Null deflection is the balance condition (A-III). Interchanging R and X and averaging removes end error (B-I). Thick copper strips have negligible resistance (C-II). The jockey is pressed gently and never slid (D-IV).

neet_phy_u20_t09_5.working: A is correct. B is wrong, because the correct form is X = R(100-l)/l. C is correct. D is correct. E is wrong, because accuracy is best near the middle. So A, C and D are correct.
